unresolved: Whether the generated content proceeds at the nominal 15 Hz pace is not established. A supporting diagnostic finds, for each generated frame k, the executed frame of the chunk (offset 0-32) with the lowest mean squared error in the same camera cell. For the left exterior camera the best offset rises with k for roughly the first 15 frames and then plateaus; the wrist-camera offsets are noisier. Cosmos3 Edge: for k = 20-32 the best offset is 14-15 (left) and 14-32 (wrist); at k = 32 it is 15 (left) and 32 (wrist); mean |best - k| is 6.2 (left) and 3.9 (wrist). FLUX 3 Action: for k = 20-32 the best offset is 15-19 (left) and 11-29 (wrist); at k = 32 it is 16 (left) and 29 (wrist); mean |best - k| is 5.2 (left) and 2.6 (wrist). A left-camera plateau fits a forecast that slows or stops relative to the execution, and equally a forecast whose later content matches no executed frame well; prediction errors confound the diagnostic, so it is inconclusive and not a timing measurement.
Generated frame 0 is a decoded reconstruction of the input, not the input itself.
FLUX 3 Action decodes with a non-causal video decoder, so each decoded frame, including frame 0, depends on the predicted latents.
Executed frames show what the simulator rendered after the controller tracked the commanded actions; they are not a target the forecast was trained to reproduce pixel for pixel.
Cosmos3 Edge decodes 528 of the 540 composite rows (exterior-cell rows 0-167 of 180); the displayed window (cell rows 57-146) lies inside the decoded region.
Only these two preselected packets were verified; nothing here establishes alignment for other packets.
observations: legend.png is drawn on first_observation.npz (tick 0) with request-0 camera transforms and is byte-identical for both packets (both episodes start from the same restored state: equal state and first-observation hashes). experiments/robolab_workshop/annotation.py draw_legend writes each number above and to the right of its circle (u+34, v-60) and draws the direction arrows afterwards, over the numbers. In the left pane the "farther" marker and the "robot-left" label cover numbers 1 (banana) and 3 (cube), and the bowl's 2 falls just below the banana circle, nearer the banana than the bowl; in the right pane the cube's 3 falls on the banana's circle.

VLM free-text observations misnumber objects in two of six labels (structured fields unaffected; all moving_object fields are 3, the cube): Cosmos3 Edge labeler A writes "1: red bowl, 2: banana", and the FLUX 3 Action adjudicator calls the cube "object 1" and the banana "object 3". Legend: 1 banana, 2 bowl, 3 cube.
Disputed fields: Cosmos3 Edge visible_final_relation (A none, B on_top_of; adjudicated none). FLUX 3 Action relation_object (A none, B 3 = the cube itself; adjudicated none).

lag_diagnostic.note: supporting only: prediction errors confound timing; not a timing proof

a.observations: The robot's gripper is shown holding a Rubik's cube (object 3) in all forecast frames. The cube is lifted and held steadily in the air, with no significant horizontal movement. The other objects (1: red bowl, 2: banana) remain stationary on the table. The gripper does not open in the final frame. No objects vanish or appear unexpectedly.

b.observations: The robot gripper is shown holding a Rubik's cube in the wrist camera view. In the exterior camera views, the Rubik's cube (object 3) is being lifted and moved. The red bowl (object 2) and yellow object (object 1) remain on the table. The gripper is holding the cube throughout the forecast frames.

adjudicated.observations: In the final frame, the wrist camera shows the gripper holding the Rubik's cube (object 3) directly above the table surface. The exterior cameras confirm the cube is suspended in the air, not touching the table or any other object. The gripper has not opened, so the cube is still held. There is no visible contact with any relation_object, so 'on_top_of' is not supported. 'none' is correct because no final spatial relation (like on_top_of, left_of, etc.) is established with any other object.
